verdict.rationale: Cursor gives engineering leads multiple concrete controls over external tool/integration access: enterprise admins can control which MCP servers users may run from the dashboard (cursor-docs-18), CLI permission tokens gate Shell/Read/Write actions including denylists (cursor-supp-cli-permissions), Run Modes (Auto-review/Allowlist/Run Everything) govern shell/MCP/Fetch calls with sandboxing (cursor-supp-run-modes), hooks can gate risky operations like beforeMCPExecution (cursor-supp-hooks), and Admin API exposes model access controls and repo blocklists (cursor-supp-admin-api). missing for 10: independent/hands-on corroboration that these admin controls work as documented in practice, and more detail on granularity of MCP allow/deny lists at the team level beyond the single doc claim.
